indicator_definition: The gender pension gap is the difference between the average pension income received by men and women aged 65 to 79, expressed as a percentage of the average pension income received by men. It reflects accumulated inequalities from the labour market, including differences in employment rates, working hours, pay and career breaks. Data are based on EU-SILC.
rationale: The gender pension gap is a consequence of lifetime inequalities in employment and earnings between men and women. Closing the gap requires addressing the root causes throughout working life, including career breaks for care responsibilities, part-time work and occupational segregation. Progress means a sustained reduction in the pension income gap between men and women.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC). Pension income includes old-age and survivors' pensions. The gender pension gap is calculated as the difference between average male and female pension incomes, expressed as a percentage of average male pension income, for persons aged 65 to 79.
